expected_shape.subject_block: the block not used by dev-a or valid-b

reveal_procedure: freeze the extractor implementation by digest and record it
verify sha256(secret) equals the commitment above
derive the corpus seed from the secret and generate sealed-c
run once; report against the thresholds already frozen
stronger_variant_not_used: seed = sha256(precommitted_secret + a future public value) would leave even the author unable to know the seed in advance. Not used here because it needs an agreed external source at reveal time; recorded so the weaker choice is visible rather than implied
what_this_still_does_not_guarantee: the author holds the secret and could reveal early. The commitment makes seed-shopping detectable, not impossible. scripts/sealed_split.py and issue #42 carry the stronger construction
why_the_corpus_is_not_materialised: not looking at a file is discipline. Not having the file is a property. The seed derives the entire corpus, so committing to its hash fixes the corpus without creating it, and it cannot be re-chosen after a result is seen — any other seed fails the commitment check
